preamble: Languages that lack the voiceless dental fricative [θ] but contrast aspirated and unaspirated stops typically map it onto the aspirated stop [tʰ] (dental [t̪ʰ] in Indo-Aryan) when adapting English words. The aspirated stop preserves the noisy, turbulent release of the fricative, which is why English /θ/ and English /t/ are kept apart: Hindi renders English t with an unaspirated stop but th with an aspirated one.
phoneticEffects: Fortition, Stopping, Addition of Aspiration, Loanword Adaptation

examples.note: English /θ/ becomes the aspirated dental stop थ, while English /t/ becomes the unaspirated retroflex ट; the Urdu spelling تَھرْما مِیٹَر shows the same aspirated reflex.
